EURO STOXX 50 Semantic Layer

The same 50 rows, with shared meaning

The EURO STOXX 50 file is a table with 9 column headings. Its meaning lives in the headings' wording and in whoever reads them. The semantic layer gives each heading a defined term from a shared vocabulary, turns text values into links, and adds the facts the table cannot hold: the full industry hierarchy, index membership, provenance and validation rules.

Select a column heading to see what it becomes. The three shaded columns on the right are not in the file: the semantic layer adds them. Select a row to open that company.

The six business questions the ontology was built to answer. Each answer below is the actual result of the SPARQL query over the graph, checked against an answer key computed independently from the CSV.

A spreadsheet accepts any value in any cell. The shapes file states what a valid company looks like. The three rows below were planted to break one rule each; all three are caught, and the 50 real companies pass.

Rules for every company

The file's "ICB Industry" column has 11 distinct values. Each company in the graph links to one 8-digit subsector, and the three levels above it come from the ICB taxonomy. Row height is one company.
